rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithāra means stirring dust or air until it leaves its place; clouds arise as winds create atmospheric moisture through interaction of heat and cold.
rows.anchor: والإثارة : تحريك القار تحريكا يضطرب به عن موضعه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basṭ means spreading, and the sky here is the upper atmosphere where clouds form.
rows.anchor: والبسط : النشر . والسماء : الجو الأعلى وهو جو الأسحبة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa is an adverbial substitute for the verbal noun of yabṣuṭu, meaning God spreads the cloud in whatever manner He wills; treating it as conditional is incorrect.
rows.anchor: وموقعها المفعولية المطلقة من { يبسطه } لأنها نائبة عن المصدر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read kisafan with kasra then fatḥa as the plural of kisf; kisfa also means a piece or fragment.
rows.anchor: و { كسفا } بكسر ففتح في قراءة الجمهور جمع كسف بكسر فسكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud is spread broadly and darkens the sky in one state, then appears as separate cloud masses in another; this variation manifests God's vast power.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنه يبسط السحاب في السماء تارة ، أي يجعله ممتدا عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in ‘you see’ is general; wadq means rain, and its channels are the gaps within either form of cloud.
rows.anchor: والودق : المطر . وضمير { خلاله } للسحاب بحالتيه المذكورتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's joy when rain falls and despair when it stops recalls God's mercy and shows His control over changing human and cloud responses.
rows.anchor: وذكر اختلاف أحوال العباد في وقت نزول المطر وفي وقت انحباسه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ‘you do not make the deaf hear’ with a second-person address to the Prophet, accusative al-ṣumm, and a feminine subject marker.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { ولا تسمع الصم } بتاء فوقية مضمومة وكسر ميم { تسمع } ونصب { الصم }

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the verb in the third person, with al-ṣumm as its nominative subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير { ولا يسمع الصم } بتحتية مفتوحة وبفتح ميم { يسمع } ورفع { الصم }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read hādī with a bāʾ and long alif, annexing it to al-ʿumī (the blind).
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { بهادي } بموحدة وبألف بعد الهاء وبإضافة { هادي } إلى { العمي } ،

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza alone reads tahdī as a direct address, without the alif, with al-ʿumī as the object.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة وحده { تهدي } بمثناة فوقية وبدون ألف بعد الهاء على الخطاب وبنصب { العمي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This fourth resumption returns to signs in creation to establish God's power and make resurrection intelligible, paralleling 30:48; the following reference to the Hour confirms the link.
rows.anchor: هذا رابع استئناف من الأربعة المتقدمة رجوع إلى الاستدلال على عظيم القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allāhu alladhī khalaqakum is the subject with its adjective, while yakhluqu mā yashāʾ is the predicate: God creates what the deniers reject.
rows.anchor: ثم قوله { الله الذي خلقكم } مبتدأ وصفة ، وقوله { يخلق ما يشاء } هو الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍaʿf with ḍamma is the more eloquent Qurashi dialect; fatḥa is also permitted in the Tamimi dialect, and weakness means frailty and softness.
rows.anchor: والضعف بضم الضاد في الآية وهو أفصح وهو لغة قريش . ويجوز في ضاده الفتح وهو لغة تميم .

rows.speaker: عبد الله ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that he recited ḍaʿf with fatḥa to the Prophet, who recited it back with ḍamma; Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī transmit the report, with no grading stated.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو داود والترمذي عن عبد الله ابن عمر قال : قرأتها على رسول الله

rows.speaker: عاصم، حمزة
rows.claim: The majority read all three occurrences with ḍamma, while ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read them with fatḥa; Ibn ʿĀshūr reconciles this with the report as dialectal allowance.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ألفاظ { ضعف } الثلاثة بضم الضاد في الثلاثة . وقرأها عاصم وحمزة بفتح الضاد ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive in origin: humans begin in a weak state as embryos and children until maturity, as if weakness were inherent in them.
rows.anchor: و { من } ابتدائية ، أي : مبتدأ خلقه من ضعف ، أي : من حالة ضعف ، وهي حالة كونه جنينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God first develops people through stages from weakness to strength and back, recreating them after death is no more extraordinary than their first creation.
rows.anchor: فكذلك ينشئكم بعد الموت إذ ليس ذلك بأعجب من الإنشاء الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development reflects wisdom, a matter of knowledge, while bringing it about in the best form is an effect of power.
rows.anchor: وذكر وصف العلم والقدرة لأن التطور هو مقتضى الحكمة وهي من شؤون العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated indefinite weakness and strength name the same kinds, not different instances; the rule that repeated indefinites differ applies when indefiniteness denotes an open individual, not a kind.
rows.anchor: ف { ضعف } المذكور ثانيا هو عين { ضعف } المذكور أولا ، و { قوة } المذكورة ثانيا عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding gray hair signals that no strength follows the final weakness and that death comes next, since gray hair is widely regarded as its herald.
rows.anchor: وعطف { وشيبة } للإيماء إلى أن هذا الضعف لا قوة بعده وأن بعده العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaybah is the verbal noun of graying, as in the description of a head bursting into gray hair.
rows.anchor: والشيبة : اسم مصدر الشيب . وقد تقدم في قوله تعالى : { واشتعل الرأس شيبا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘its punishment’ refers to Hell, encompassing both fire and the reported punishment of intense cold, zamharīr.
rows.anchor: وضمير { عذابها } عائد إلى جهنم ليشمل ما ورد من أن المعذبين يعذبون بالنار ويعذبون بالزمهرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kathālika functions as an absolute object of najzī: God requites them with such a requital; the phrase about every ungrateful disbeliever is a concluding generalization.
rows.anchor: ووقع { كذلك } موقع المفعول المطلق لقوله : { نجزي } أي نجزيهم جزاء كذلك الجزاء ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaffūr means one intensely unbelieving, namely a polytheist.
rows.anchor: والكفور : الشديد الكفر ، وهو المشرك .

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read najzī with the first-person plural and accusative kulla.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { نجزي } بنون العظمة ونصب { كل } .

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads yujzā in the passive, with kulla as nominative subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو عمرو وحده { يجزى } بياء الغائب والبناء للنائب ورفع { كل } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to those who disbelieved in 35:36, and the clause is coordinated with ‘they have the Fire of Hell’; it is not circumstantial because the preceding conclusion closes that discourse.
rows.anchor: الضمير إلى { الذين كفروا } ( فاطر : 36 ) والجملة عطف على جملة { لهم نار جهنم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūn intensifies yaṣrukhūn: they scream with great effort because of what has befallen them; their plea explains the screaming and displays their helplessness.
rows.anchor: و { يصطرخون } مبالغة في ( يصرخون ) لأنه افتعال من الصراخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to do good if released is belated repentance; the jussive yaʿmal ṣāliḥan answers the plea with the understood condition ‘if You release us.’
rows.anchor: ولإرادة الوعد جزم { نعمل صالحا } في جواب الدعاء . والتقدير : إن تخرجنا نعمل صالحا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their future deeds different from what they did before expresses regret: they now know their former deeds were false and harmful in the realm of realities.
rows.anchor: وهذا ندامة على ما كانوا يعملونه لأنهم أيقنوا بفساد عملهم وضره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿmīr is prolonging a life; the related expression ‘a time’ is a temporal, masdar-based adverbial phrase.
rows.anchor: والتعمير : تطويل العمر . وقد تقدم غير مرة ، منها عند قوله تعالى : { يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘whoever reflects in it’ describes a span of time sufficient for reflection and instruction.
rows.anchor: أي زمانا كافيا بامتداده للتذكر والتبصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warner is Muhammad; calling him a warner highlights the aspect of his mission most relevant to these people.
rows.anchor: و { النذير } الرسول محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Your warner came’ coordinates with the preceding question because it conveys an assertion; coordinating an assertion with an interrogative form is valid here.
rows.anchor: لأن معناها الخبر فعطف عليها الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in ‘taste’ marks consequence, its object ‘the punishment’ is omitted, and the imperative conveys their continuing punishment and inability to escape.
rows.anchor: والفاء في { فذوقوا } للتفريع . وحذف مفعول ( ذوقوا ) لدلالة المقام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The wrongdoers have no helper’ may continue the rebuke, ending their hope of rescue and asking where their supposed allies are.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون من جملة الكلام الذي وبخهم الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it is a separate conclusion for listeners, making the rule apply to every wrongdoer, including the disbelievers just described.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كلاما مستقلا مفرعا على القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoing violates a rights-holder's due; its gravest form is shirk, an assault on God's oneness and on the self by leading it into punishment.
rows.anchor: وأعظمه الشرك لأنه اعتداء على الله بإنكار صفته النفيسة وهي الوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generality of wrongdoers and helpers means helping an oppressor violates justice; the community must restrain wrongdoing, refuting the pre-Islamic maxim to help one's brother whether wrongdoer or victim.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا إبطال لخلق أهل الجاهلية القائلين في أمثالهم ( انصر أخاك ظالما أو مظلوما ) .

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet corrected that maxim: helping an unjust person means restraining him from his injustice.
rows.anchor: إذا كان ظالما تنصره على نفسه فتكفه عن ظلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God knows the unseen links His knowledge of believers and servants to the next argument about the alleged partners, while recapping the earlier proof of His care and knowledge.
rows.anchor: جملة { إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض } استئناف واصل بين جملة { إن الله بعباده لخبير بصير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repays each person according to the intention concealed within; the passage presents this as an implication of His knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا إيماء إلى أن الله يجازي كل ذي نية على حسب ما أضمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of what is in people's hearts follows from His knowledge of the unseen, since hidden matters include their inner states.
rows.anchor: لأن ما في الصدور من الأمور المغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhāt al-ṣudūr means people's inner thoughts and intentions.
rows.anchor: و ( ذات الصدور ) ضمائر الناس ونياتهم ، وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { إنه عليم بذات الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participle ʿālim and emphatic ʿalīm differ rhetorically: the latter stresses that nothing escapes God's knowledge, indirectly pointing to requital.
rows.anchor: وجيء في الإخبار بعلم الله بالغيب بصيغة اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He is the One who made you successors on earth’ is parenthetical between the statement of God's knowledge and the consequence for disbelief.
rows.anchor: وجملة هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض } معترضة بين جملة { إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض } الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalāʾif means successors: one possibility is that later human generations followed earlier peoples, including all groups, which also shows that God knows those He created.
rows.anchor: والخلائف : جمع خليفة ، وهو الذي يخلف غيره في أمر كان لذلك الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, khalāʾif means people given authority over the earth; Ibn ʿĀshūr reads this as good news of Muslim political rule and Islam's eventual ascendancy.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : هو الذي جعلكم متصرفين في الأرض ، كقوله تعالى : { ويستخلفكم في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence strengthens the assertion that God made the addressees successors on earth.
rows.anchor: والجملة الاسمية مفيدة تقوي الحكم الذي هو جعل الله المخاطبين خلائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional ‘whoever disbelieves, his disbelief is against him’ indirectly signals that God does not depend on their ceasing to disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وهو شرط مستعمل كناية عن عدم الاهتمام بأمر دوامهم على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about increased contempt explains the preceding clause but is coordinated as an independent assertion to emphasize it.
rows.anchor: وإنما خولف ذلك للدلالة على الاهتمام بهذا البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqt is hatred mixed with humiliation; God's ‘hatred’ figuratively means withdrawing His grace and imposing severe punishment.
rows.anchor: والمقت : البغض مع خزي وصغار ، وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا وساء سبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent paradox is resolved by taking repeated disbelief as persistence over time: the polytheists boasted they would not follow Muslims, and God answers that their continued disbelief increases contempt and loss.
rows.anchor: فتأويل الآية : أنهم لما وصفوا بالكفر ابتداء ثم أخبر بأن كفرهم يزيدهم مقتا علم أن المراد بكفرهم الثاني

rows.speaker: صاحب التقريب
rows.claim: One proposed argument says that if God wanted offspring as claimed, He would choose males, considered superior, rather than females; al-Taftāzānī calls this the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: وبنى عليه صاحب ( التقريب ) فقال عقب تعقب كلام ( الكشاف ) ( والأولى ما قيل : لو أراد أن يتخذ ولدا كما زعمتم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya adopts an argument closer and clearer than al-Kashshāf's, but Ibn ʿĀshūr says it still fails to connect the verse with its context.
rows.anchor: والذي سلكه ابن عطية وإن كان أقرب وأوضح من مسلك ( الكشاف ) في تقرير الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Glory be to Him’ disavows the alleged partners after the impossibility argument and returns to the address to the Prophet and Muslims begun at 39:2.
rows.anchor: وجملة { سبحانه } تنزيه له عما نسبوه إليه من الشركاء بعد أن أبطله بالدليل الامتناعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He is God, the One, the Overpowering’ proves the disavowal: oneness negates every kind of divine partner, and overpowering negates the claim that idols intercede or bring people near.
rows.anchor: وإثبات الوحدانية له يبطل الشريك في الإلاهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qahr means dominance: nothing can overcome God or deflect Him from His will.
rows.anchor: والقهر : الغلبة ، أي هو الشديد الغلبة لكل شيء لا يغلبه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth explains God's oneness and irresistible power, and establishes that He alone creates, since the alleged partners cannot create the worlds.
rows.anchor: وقد انتقل من الاستدلال باقتضاء حقيقة الإلاهية نفي الشريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq means creation is joined to truth and wisdom, against purposelessness, with soundness and benefit rather than disorder.
rows.anchor: والباء في { بالحق } للملابسة ، أي خلقها خلقا ملابسا للحق وهو هنا ضد العبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense yūkawwir suggests repeated renewal or evokes the action through its recurring effects, since the process itself is unseen.
rows.anchor: وأوثر المضارع في هذه الجملة للدلالة على تجدد ذلك وتكرره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takwīr literally means wrapping; the alternation of night and day over earth is pictured as successive folds of a turban, with earth as the head.
rows.anchor: والتكوير حقيقته : اللف واللي ، يقال : كور العمامة على رأسه إذا لواها ولفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because takwīr derives from a round ball, Ibn ʿĀshūr reads the wording as a scientific allusion to Earth's sphericity, unknown to Arabs and most people then.
rows.anchor: فإن مادة التكوير جائية من اسم الكرة ، وهي الجسم المستدير من جميع جهاته على التساوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of takwīr suits this proof of divinity through creation and anticipates later Muslim astronomy; 7:54 instead uses ‘cover’ to show God's broad control over created qualities.
rows.anchor: لأن تلك الآية مسوقة للدلالة على سعة التصرف في المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about rolling day over night is a coordinated part of the intended assertion, like the paired description in 66:5.
rows.anchor: وعطف جملة { ويكور النهار على الليل } هو من عطف الجزء المقصود من الخبر كقوله : { ثيبات وأبكارا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subjugating the sun and moon means directing their ordered courses; this is coordinated because the day-night alternation results from that subjugation.
rows.anchor: وتسخير الشمس والقمر هو تذليلهما للعمل على ما جعل الله لهما من نظام السير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Each runs for a term’ is an inclusive apposition clarifying the subjugation; kull is compensatory for ‘each one,’ and running means swift movement.
rows.anchor: وجملة { كل يجري لأجلل مسمى } في موقع بدل اشتمال من جملة { سخر الشمس والقمر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term may be the end of the sun and moon: their motion advances their eventual extinction, as with the sun's course to its resting place.
rows.anchor: والأجل هو أجل فنائهما فإن جريهما لما كان فيه تقريب فنائهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the term may be human lifespans, measured by the periods and breaths tracked through the sun and moon's motion.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالأجل أجل حياة الناس

rows.speaker: أسقف نجران
rows.claim: A bishop of Najran's verse uses the sun's changing course as evidence against permanence.
rows.anchor: قال أسقف نجران : منع البقاء تقلب الشمس وطلوعها من حيث لا تمسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ajl al-musammā is what God marked out; ‘for a term’ and ‘to a term’ are close in basic meaning, and the differing prepositions may simply vary the expression.
rows.anchor: والمسمى : المجعول له وسم ، أي ما به يعين وهو ما عينه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz warns that God does what He wills and cannot be overcome; al-Ghaffār invites repentance through Islam, especially before death ends the chance to repent.
rows.anchor: فإن وصف { العزيز } كناية عن أنه يفعل ما يشاء لا غالب له فلا تجدي المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning forgiveness alongside the appointed term urges people to repent before death, when recovery is no longer possible; the opening alert marks the statement's importance.
rows.anchor: وفي وصف الغفار } مناسبة لذكر الأجل لأن المغفرة يظهر أثرها بعد البعث الذي يكون بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse turns to the remarkable creation of humanity, including the single original soul and Adam's spouse, whose creation enables procreation.
rows.anchor: انتقال إلى الاستدلال بخلق الناس وهو الخلق العجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human-creation clause may be circumstantial from the mention of God or a fresh, repeated proof; its address to polytheists shifts from third to second person for indirect and direct argument together.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للمشركين بدليل قوله بعده : { فأنى تصرفون } ، وهو التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks rank, not chronology: creating Adam's spouse from himself is an independent and more astonishing proof than the creation of descendants, unlike the blessing-focused sequence in 7:189.
rows.anchor: لأن زمن خلق زوج آدم سابق على خلق الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to confront the polytheists addresses those who pressed the Prophet to abandon his call and follow their religion; context identifies the two groups addressed.
rows.anchor: هذا القول متعين لأن يكون الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمورا بأن يواجه به المشركين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil reports that Quraysh asked the Prophet what led him to this religion and urged him to follow the faith of his fathers and leaders.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم قول مقاتل : قال كفار قريش للنبيء : ما يحملك على هذا الدين الذي أتيتنا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating ‘say’ and the declaration of worshipping God alone reinforces 39:11: the two formulations each imply exclusivity and together establish it three times, preparing the warning that follows.
rows.anchor: أمر بأن يعيد التصريح بأنه يعبد الله وحده تأكيدا لقوله : { قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ introduces a rhetorical consequence, and ‘worship whatever you wish besides Him’ is a leave-it-to-you challenge showing indifference; their choice rests on whim, not evidence.
rows.anchor: والأمر في قوله : { فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه } مستعمل في معنى التخلية ، ويعبر عنه بالتسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the apparent leave-taking, the Qur'an adds admonition indirectly, speaking of the addressees as absent while intending them.
rows.anchor: أعقب أمر التسوية في شأنهم بشيء من الموعظة حرصا على إصلاحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic opening and definite ‘the losers’ make the phrase a hyperbolic restriction: complete losers are those who lose themselves and their families.
rows.anchor: وافتتح المقول بحرف التوكيد تنبيها على أنه واقع وتعريف { الخاسرين } تعريف الجنس ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contextual target is the polytheists under debate; the relative clause replaces direct address to warn that they will lose themselves and their families at Judgment.
rows.anchor: علم أن المراد بالذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم هم الذين جرى الجدال معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Losing oneself pictures people causing their own punishment while imagining they are securing bliss, like a merchant whose capital is ruined; the wording also occurs in 7:9.
rows.anchor: ومعنى خسرانهم أنفسهم : أنهم تسببوا لأنفسهم في العذاب في حين حسبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose their families by leading spouses and children into disbelief, so neither they nor their relatives benefit or help one another in the next life.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم أغروا أهليهم من أزواجهم وأولادهم بالكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding ‘that is the manifest loss’ draws the result: losing one's dearest things makes their loss the greatest and clearest, emphasized by the verbal noun al-khusrān.
rows.anchor: ولذلك أوثرت خسارتهم باسم الخسران الذي هو اسم مصدر الخسارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative, attention particle, and separating pronoun heighten and rhetorically restrict the judgment of their loss.
rows.anchor: وبتوسط ضمير الفصل المفيد للقصر وهو قصر ادعائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of fire-canopies is an appositional explanation of the manifest loss, singling out bodily destruction as its harshest part; disgrace, divine anger, and lost hope are also included.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين } ( الزمر : 15 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓulal means raised coverings; here it metaphorically describes layers over the people of Hell, ironically named shade because they seek shelter from heat but receive none.
rows.anchor: وهي هنا استعارة للطبقة التي تعلو أهل النار في نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat may conclude the warning or answer why punishment is prepared: God describes it to warn people during life and direct them to follow His law; by contrast, Paradise is made to encourage piety.
rows.anchor: تذييل للتهديد بالوعيد من قوله تعالى : { قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم } ( الزمر : 15 ) الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says Paradise apparently existed before the obligations as a home for purified souls, while Hell may already exist or may be created on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الجنة جعلها الله مسكنا لأهل النفوس المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says Hell complained that its parts consumed one another, so God allowed it two breaths, one in winter and one in summer; Ibn ʿĀshūr says it suggests prior creation but can be interpreted otherwise.
rows.anchor: وهو ظاهر حديث : ( اشتكت النار إلى ربها فقالت : أكل بعضي بعضا فأذن لها بنفسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The layers beneath the inhabitants are also called canopies by associative wordplay, because they shelter other unbelievers in Hell's many levels.
rows.anchor: وأما إطلاق الظلل على الطبقات التي تحتهم فهو من باب المشاكلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat Ghāfir is Meccan by consensus, apart from a view attributed to al-Ḥasan that excludes this verse.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق وعن الحسن استثناء قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan thought the command to glorify God at evening and morning was revealed concerning the five prescribed prayers and their times, which he placed in Medina; in Mecca he believed only two untimed rakʿahs daily were required.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن استثناء قوله تعالى : { وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار } ( غافر : 55 ) ، لأنه كان يرى أنها نزلت في فرض الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects that view as resting on a weak premise: most scholars place the five prayers and their times in Mecca, and tasbīḥ can retain its ordinary sense of glorification rather than refer to ritual prayer.
rows.anchor: وهو من بناء ضعيف على ضعيف فإن الجمهور على أن الصلوات الخمس فرضت بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Moses interrupts 40:51 before the command to be patient; deliverance from subjection into independent rule parallels the Muslims and hints that the Qur'an will endure in their community.
rows.anchor: فجملة : { ولقد ءاتينا موسى الهدى } الخ معترضة بين { إنا لننصر رسلنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's guidance comprises his prophetic mission and the Torah's law; Israel inherited the law, not his unique messengerhood, and ‘inheritance’ means it remained among them after his death.
rows.anchor: والهدى الذي أوتيه موسى هو ما أوحي إليه من الأمر بالدعوة إلى الدين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording compresses the sense ‘We gave Moses guidance and the Book, and made Israel inherit the Book’; the Torah is one part of his guidance.
rows.anchor: ففي الكلام إيجاز حذف تقديره : ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى والكتاب وأورثنا بني إسرائيل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan and dhikrā are circumstantial descriptions of the Book: it teaches what learners did not know and reminds its learned readers of what they know, including juristic derivation by scholars.
rows.anchor: و { هدى } و { ذكرى } حالان من { الكتاب ، } أي هدى لبني إسرائيل وذكرى لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be patient follows from God's promise to support His messengers: the Prophet should know God supports him and the believers and should not weaken.
rows.anchor: تفريع على قوله : { إنا لننصر رسلنا } ( غافر : 51 ) أي فاعلم أنا ناصروك والذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna emphasizes the promise and serves a causal role in the command to be patient; God's promise of victory is true, so the Prophet should not hasten it.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { إن وعد الله حق } تعليل للأمر بالصبر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised victory came at Badr, the conquest of Mecca, Ḥunayn, and other campaigns; Uḥud's setback tested believers and warned against disobeying the Prophet's order to hold position, before the final outcome favored them.
rows.anchor: وذلك ما نصر به النبي في أيامه على المشركين يوم بدر ويوم الفتح ويوم حنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness and glorification follow patience as signs of gratitude, indirectly showing victory is certain; the Prophet seeks continued protection and forgiveness as worship and proper conduct, while the community is all the more urged to do so.
rows.anchor: وعطف على الأمر بالصبر الأمر بالاستغفار والتسبيح فكانا داخلين في سياق التفريع على الوعد بالنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evening and morning stand for all times: evening runs from late day into night, and ibkār is the morning's first part; glorification completes inner and outer gratitude.
rows.anchor: أي الأوقات كلها فاقتصر على طرفي أوقات العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the command after victory in Sūrat al-Naṣr, this command includes patience because the Prophet is still awaiting promised victory; after victory, the focus is pure gratitude.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك مقام محض الشكر دون الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istijābah means answering a caller; by extension it means obeying what the Prophet conveys from God, so people must obey before the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: وأطلقت الاستجابة على امتثال ما يطالبهم به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تبليغا عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-rabbikum marks the recipient and strengthens transitivity; the underlying form is istajābahu lah, as in the construction in 2:186.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لربكم } لتأكيد تعدية الفعل إلى المفعول مثل : حمدت له وشكرت له

rows.speaker: كعب الغنوي
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Ghanawī's couplet supplies poetic evidence for istajāba li, including the form lam yastajibhu.
rows.anchor: قال كعب الغنوي : وداعع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marrad is a verbal noun meaning return; ‘no return’ says the Day cannot be reversed. Min Allāh can attach to ‘comes’ or to the predicate, but not directly complete marrad, which would make lā's noun quasi-annexed and inflected rather than built on fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والمرد : مصدر بمعنى الرد ، وتقدم آنفا في قوله : { هل إلى مرد من سبيل } ( الشورى : 44 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maljaʾ literally means a refuge, but here it figuratively means a protector who can shield people from punishment.
rows.anchor: ويطلق مجازا على الناصر ، وهو المراد هنا ، أي ما لكم من شيء يقيكم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakīr is a verbal noun: on that Day people will have no grounds to deny what they receive and can only acknowledge it.
rows.anchor: والنكير : اسم مصدر أنكر ، أي ما لكم إنكار لما جوزيتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequence of the prior call to respond gathers up the whole earlier command to invite them to faith, then consoles the Prophet if they turn away.
rows.anchor: الفاء للتفريع على قوله : { استجيبوا لربكم } ( الشورى : 47 ) الآية ، وهو جامع لما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from direct address to ‘if they turn away’ echoes the opening statement that God is their guardian and the Prophet is not their keeper; otherwise it would say ‘if you turn away.’
rows.anchor: وهذا الارتباط هو نكتة الالتفات من الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We did not send you as their keeper’ indicates the omitted conditional result rather than serving as it: the Prophet bears no blame for refusal, since his only duty is to convey.
rows.anchor: ليس هو جواب الشرط في المعنى ولكنه دليل عليه ، وقائم مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who expect the afterlife to preserve their worldly comfort do so from desire, not evidence; the ensuing question expresses amazement and treats their condition as plainly visible.
rows.anchor: قالوا ذلك عن غير دليل ولا نظر ولكن عن اتباع ما يشتهون لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question's original order placed the interrogative first; its address may be to the Prophet and Muslims or general, since their condition is obvious to any observer.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم والمقصود من معه من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative expression refers to mockers who assume life and death are confined to this world, as indicated by the following plural report of their speech.
rows.anchor: و { من } الموصولة صادقة على فريق المستهزئين الذين حسبوا أن يكون محياهم ومماتهم سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their argument is appetite and sophistry, not proof; they resist guidance because they have been habituated to desire, leaving faculties unable to benefit from warnings and signs of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { أضله الله } أنه حفهم بأسباب الضلالة من عقول مكابرة ونفوس ضعيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilāhahu may mean an obeyed object treated like a deity, making desire the master; alternatively, desire means what they love, and they worship idols through attachment and habit.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يبقى { إلاهه } على الحقيقة ويكون { هواه } بمعنى مهويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This statement follows the argument in 45:21: their claim that their fate would be better was provocation, not belief in resurrection; their actual belief is that there is no life after death.
rows.anchor: أي بعد أن جادلوا المسلمين بأنه إن كان يبعث بعد الموت فستكون عقباهم خيرا من عقبى المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hiyā may be the pronoun of the story, meaning the whole question of resurrection reduces to denying life after death; alternatively it refers elliptically to life, restricting life to this world.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { هي } ضمير الحياة باعتبار دلالة الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We die and live’ explains that no other world follows: some die while others remain or are born, and the present tense depicts recurring change; it cannot mean resurrection because the prior clause excludes it.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { نموت ونحيا } يموت بعضنا ويحيا بعض أي يبقى حيا إلى أمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be their actual proverb or a Qur'anic concise rendering of ‘some die and others live’; waw does not imply chronological order.
rows.anchor: والعطف بالواو لا يقتضي ترتيبا بين المتعاطفين في الحصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is placed first to stress their claim that it ends life; it also creates the contrasts between worldly life and death, then death and life, with the cadence following that emphasis.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن تقديم فعل { نموت } على { نحيا } للاهتمام بالموت في هذا المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says they have no knowledge that time itself kills, since they offer no evidence for that claim.
rows.anchor: فالإشارة ب { ذلك } إلى قولهم { وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر } ، أي لا علم لهم بأن الدهر هو المميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying time alone destroys them, they confine life and death to this world: life comes through formation and death through the passage of time, aging, or destructive causes.
rows.anchor: وأما زيادة { وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر } فقصدوا تأكيد معنى انحصار الحياة والموت في هذا العالم

rows.speaker: عمرو بن قميئة
rows.claim: The old poet ʿAmr ibn Qumayʾa speaks of the daughters of time striking from where he cannot see, illustrating the personification of time as an agent.
rows.anchor: ومن الشعر القديم قول عمرو بن قميئة : رمتني بنات الدهر من حيث لا أرى

rows.speaker: أسقف نجران
rows.claim: The bishop of Najran likewise attributes impermanence to the sun's turning and rising, another poetic formulation about time and mortality.
rows.anchor: كما قال أسقف نجران : منع البقاء تقلب الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conventional claim reflects little inquiry, despite their knowing God created the worlds; time is an abstract measure of intervals and seasons, so it cannot directly or indirectly cause death.
rows.anchor: إذ الزمان أمر اعتباري لا يفعل ولا يؤثر وإنما هو مقادير يقدر بها الناس الأبعاد بين الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference in ‘they have no knowledge of that’ is specifically their claim that time causes death; their basis is mere supposition or imaginative conjecture.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالظن في قوله : { إن هم إلا يظنون } ما ليس بعلم
